items.name: UIAPI
items.doc: Game UI: widget events, focus, text measurement. Widgets are the components Panel, Button, Toggle, Slider, TextField and ScrollList (see docs/SCRIPTING.md, UI); TouchStick and TouchButton, the on-screen gamepad, send no events: they press gamepad bindings (docs/MOBILE.md). The UI keeps working while time.scale is 0.

members.sig: measureText(text: string, opts?: { fontSize?: number; font?: string; maxWidth?: number; space?: "screen" | "world"; maxTextScale?: number; autoShrink?: boolean; minFontSize?: number; maxHeight?: number; markup?: boolean; bold?: boolean }): { width: number; height: number; fontSize: number }
members.doc: Size of `text` laid out exactly like Text rendering: shaped (ligatures, kerning, Arabic joining, bidi) and wrapped at maxWidth > 0 at spaces and between CJK characters. `space` (default "screen") says how it will be drawn: a "screen" label is measured at fontSize * ui.textScale, a "world" one is not scaled. Headless runs approximate 0.6 * fontSize per character (with a warning). maxTextScale, autoShrink, minFontSize and maxHeight are the fields of Text with the same names: the size is capped, and shrunk to fit maxWidth x maxHeight, exactly as a Text with them is drawn. `fontSize` in the result is the size it is laid out at, in pixels (fontSize times the capped text scale, or the shrunk size). The result is in UI units, like the sizes of widgets: ui.scale is not applied (ui.rectOf, which is in screen pixels, includes it). `markup` and `bold` are the fields of Text with the same names: with `markup: true` the tags are not characters, [b] and [icon:name] are measured as drawn (an icon is as tall as the line; headless it counts as two characters), and the project's "text" section (factoria.json) says which colours and icons exist. Example: ui.measureText("[b]3[/b] [icon:fish]", { fontSize: 20, markup: true }).width.

What is wrong with the markup of `text`, as a Text with `markup: true` would read it: an unknown tag, a "[" without "]", an unclosed [b] or [c:], a [c:name] or [icon:name] the "text" section of factoria.json does not define (with a "did you mean"). [] when it is clean. The text is still drawn (a bad tag is shown as written), so a test can walk every string of the game and fail with the list. Example: expect(ui.markupProblems("[b]Sold[/b] [icon:fish]")).toEqual([]);

true when the text of a screen-space or world Text with a box (maxWidth, maxHeight) or the label of a Button, Toggle, Slider or TouchButton still does not fit its box at the size it is drawn at, i.e. after ui.textScale, maxTextScale and autoShrink (down to minFontSize) have done what they can. false for any other entity, an empty text or a Text without a box. Read it after game.step or ui.layout(). Same as `overflowed: true` in `ui.state`. Example: ui.textScale = 2; game.step(1); expect(ui.overflowed("play_button")).toBe(false);

Where a UI widget, an Interactable (a world-space one as its camera shows it) or a screen-space Text is drawn, as { x, y, w, h } in design pixels: (x, y) is the TOP-LEFT corner and y grows downwards (like screen.safeArea, unlike entity.bounds()). It includes the safe area, the interface scale (ui.scale: at 1.5 a widget of size 100 is 150 wide) and what a Panel or ScrollList laid out, so read it after game.step or ui.layout(). Takes an Entity or an id/name; null for an entity that is neither (a world-space sprite) and for one that is hidden, by itself or by an inactive parent (`activeInHierarchy` false), like `ui.state`, which does not list it. Same numbers as the rect of `ui.state`. Example: const r = ui.rectOf("options.panel"); expect(r.x + r.w).toBeLessThan(1280);

Runs the UI layout now, exactly what every frame does: autoSize sizes, fit sizes, ScrollList fill, positions and the Panel fallbackLayout choice. After changing a label or a font size, call it and read Button.size, Panel.size or ui.rectOf right away, with no game.step. Throws when the run has no UI system. Example: button.get("Button").text = "A longer label"; ui.layout(); const w = ui.rectOf(button).w;

members.sig: readonly dragging: { source: Entity | null; payload: any; from: { x: number; y: number }; x: number; y: number; target: Entity | null; accepts: boolean } | null
members.doc: The drag in progress, or null: truthy exactly while a draggable widget is being dragged (from the dragStart event until drop or dragCancel). A script that reads the pointer for the world can test `if (ui.dragging) return;` so a drag that began on the UI does not also click the map. `from` is where the press was; x, y the pointer now; target and accepts as in the events.

members.sig: setDropTarget(target: Entity | string, rule: boolean | ((drag: { source: Entity | null; payload: any; x: number; y: number }) => boolean) | null): void
members.doc: Says whether a widget takes drops: true, false, or a function asked every frame while a drag is over it (it returns true to accept; use it to colour the target), or null to remove the rule. A widget with no rule refuses; the nearest ancestor with a rule counts for its children, so one rule on a Panel covers its Buttons. Rules end with the scene. Example: ui.setDropTarget(\"slot_1\", (d) => canAssign(d.payload)).

members.sig: setWorldDropTarget(rule: boolean | ((drag: { source: Entity | null; payload: any; x: number; y: number }) => boolean) | null): void
members.doc: Says whether a drop over no widget (the map) is accepted: true by default, false refuses (the drag ends with dragCancel reason \"rejected\"), a function can look at the world at (x, y). null goes back to the default. Ends with the scene.

Makes a widget follow the pointer during the drag, its centre under the pointer; hit tests, hover and drop targets ignore it. Call it from the dragStart handler (the engine moves it from the next frame on). The engine only moves it: hide or destroy it in the drop and dragCancel handlers. null stops it.
Ends the drag in progress with a dragCancel event (reason \"script\"). Does nothing when nothing is dragged.

members.sig: showTooltip(content: string | { title?: string; lines?: Array<string | { text: string; color?: string | number[] }>; args?: object }, at?: { x: number; y: number }): void
members.doc: Shows a tooltip now, for something that is not a widget (a map tile, a chart point). `content` is a string or { title, lines, args }; each text is a localization key when localization is on and has it, else it is shown as written. `at` is a screen position in design pixels (default: the pointer); the box is placed next to it and flipped to stay on screen, like the tooltip of a widget, and styled by the "ui" section of factoria.json (tooltip). It stays until ui.hideTooltip(), until the pointer moves more than 5 pixels from where it was at the call, or until a scene loads. Throws on a content that is not a string or an object. Example: ui.showTooltip({ title: "Harbour", lines: ["Docks: 3"] }, { x: 400, y: 300 }).
Hides the tooltip at once, whatever showed it (a widget, a script function or ui.showTooltip). A tooltip of a widget shows again only after the pointer rests again.

members.sig: setTooltip(target: Entity | string, tooltip: string | { title?: string; lines?: Array<string | { text: string; color?: string | number[] }>; args?: object } | ((entity: Entity) => string | object | null) | null): void
members.doc: Sets the tooltip of a widget or Panel. Static content is written to the `tooltip` field of its UI component; a function is called when the tooltip is about to show (and each frame while it shows) and returns the content, or null for no tooltip, so it can read the game state; it ends with the scene. null removes the tooltip. A tooltip shows after ui.tooltipDelay seconds of rest within 5 pixels, on the first widget under the pointer or its ancestors that has one. Example: ui.setTooltip("buy", () => ({ title: "Buy", lines: [`${price} coins`] })).

members.sig: setWorldTooltip(fn: ((x: number, y: number) => string | object | null) | null): void
members.doc: Sets a function asked for a tooltip when the pointer rests over no widget; it gets the pointer in design pixels and returns the content or null. Its tooltip has source "world". null removes it. It ends with the scene.

members.sig: readonly tooltip: { title: string; lines: string[]; rect: number[]; source: "widget" | "script" | "world" | "manual"; widget: string | null } | null
members.doc: The tooltip that shows now, or null: its title, its lines, its rect [x, y, w, h] in screen pixels (with the interface scale), what showed it (source) and the entity id of the widget for "widget" and "script". Same as `tooltip` in ui.state. Read it after game.step.

Seconds the pointer rests before a tooltip shows, 0 to 60 (default: tooltipDelay of the "ui" section of factoria.json, 0.5). The rest is counted with the game's UI time, so tests with game.step are exact. Setting a number outside 0 to 60 throws. Resets to the project value for every test file.

The player's text size option, 0.5 to 3 (default 1): the font size of every screen-space Text (space "screen") and of the labels of Button, Toggle, Slider and TextField is multiplied by it, and ui.measureText (space "screen") agrees. World-space Text, and its entity.bounds(), are not scaled. Widgets keep their rectangles and wrapped text keeps its maxWidth, so leave room for the biggest size you offer (ui.scale makes room by growing the whole interface). Setting a number outside 0.5 to 3 throws; clamp a saved value first. A change sends the "textScale" event (ui.on). The engine does not save it: keep it in `storage` and set it at start. Resets to 1 for every test file. Same as the ui.set_text_scale command.

The interface scale, 0.5 to 3 (1 = as authored). Every screen-space widget (Panel, Button, Toggle, Slider, TextField, ScrollList, ...) and screen-space Text, Sprite and Shape2D is laid out in UI units and drawn this many times as big: size, offset, padding, spacing, margins and font size (ui.textScale comes on top of it for text). Anchors do not move: a widget anchored to a corner stays in it. ui.rectOf, ui.state and the hit test are in screen pixels, so they include it. A game starts at the `ui.scale` of factoria.json (default 1); the menu kit's Options has an Interface size row. Setting a number outside 0.5 to 3 throws; clamp a saved value first. A change sends the "scale" event (ui.on). The engine does not save it: keep it in `storage` and set it at start. Resets to the project default for every test file. Same as the ui.set_scale command. Example: ui.scale = 1.5; ui.layout(); expect(ui.rectOf("panel").w).toBe(1.5 * 320);

Whether the screen-space UI is mirrored in a right-to-left language (i18n.direction "rtl"), default: mirrorRtl of the "ui" section of factoria.json (true). Mirrored: anchor.x, pivot.x and position.x of every widget (and the Text, Sprite and Shape2D under it) flip, so a Panel anchored left sits on the right; Toggle boxes sit at the right of their label and Sliders run right to left (a click, the arrow keys and the fill follow). A widget with UiBox.mirror false (and its children) stays as authored. ui.rectOf and ui.state report the mirrored rectangles. Not saved by the engine; resets to the project value for every test file. Same as the ui.set_mirror_rtl command.

Listens to a change of ui.scale ("scale") or ui.textScale ("textScale"), like i18n.on("change"): the callback gets { type, value, previous }, once per change to another value, with the game events of the frame (after the code that changed the option has returned). Use it to rebuild what depends on the size of the interface: ui.on("scale", () => { ui.layout(); relayout(); }). Returns the function that stops listening; listeners end with the scene, like ui.on. There is no target: these events are about no widget.

Listens to the pointer moving over the samples of a Chart (a bar, or the nearest point of a line): the callback gets { type, id, entity, index, series, value } each time the sample under the pointer changes, and index -1 when the pointer leaves the chart. Returns the function that stops listening; listeners end with the scene.

members.sig: on(type: "chartHover", target: Entity | string, fn: (e: UiChartEvent) => void): () => void
members.doc: Like on("chartHover", fn) for one Chart, e.g. ui.on("chartHover", "sales_chart", (e) => showDay(e.index)).

Listens to the pointer over a CameraView: the callback gets { type, id, entity, phase, x, y, u, v, dx, dy, wheel } on a press ("down"), while the button is held and the pointer moves ("drag"), on the release ("up") and when the wheel turns over the view ("wheel"). Use it to turn or zoom what the view shows: ui.on("viewPointer", (e) => { if (e.phase === "drag") yaw += e.dx * 0.7; }). Returns the function that stops listening; listeners end with the scene.

members.sig: on(type: "viewPointer", target: Entity | string, fn: (e: UiViewPointerEvent) => void): () => void
members.doc: Like on("viewPointer", fn) for one CameraView, e.g. ui.on("viewPointer", "item_view", (e) => turn(e)).

Listens to the steps of a drag that began on a widget with `draggable` (UiBox.draggable): dragStart, dragOver, drop (released over a target that accepts: a widget with a rule from ui.setDropTarget, or the world) and dragCancel (rejected, cancelled with ui_cancel, the source gone or ui.cancelDrag()). The event has the source, its payload, the pointer (x, y) and the target (null over the world). Returns the function that stops listening; listeners end with the scene.

members.sig: on(type: "dragStart" | "dragOver" | "drop" | "dragCancel", target: Entity | string, fn: (e: UiDragEvent) => void): () => void
members.doc: Like on(type, fn) for one widget: for dragStart and dragCancel `target` is the dragged widget, for dragOver and drop it is the drop target, e.g. ui.on("drop", "slot_1", (e) => assign(e.payload)).

members.sig: on(type: "click" | "change" | "submit" | "focus" | "blur" | "hover" | "press" | "release" | "cancel", fn: (e: UiEvent) => void | boolean): () => void
members.doc: Listens to a widget event from any widget. A "cancel" handler that returns true handled the press: input.consume("ui_cancel") is called for it, so the same Escape does not also read as pressed for "pause" or any action on that key later in the frame (Escape closes a dialog and the pause menu stays shut). The click of a focused Button or Toggle pressed by ui_submit is consumed by the UI itself. Returns the function that stops listening. Inside a behaviour prefer this.on("ui.click", (data, source) => ...), which is removed with the behaviour. An unknown type throws with a suggestion.

members.sig: on(type: "click" | "change" | "submit" | "focus" | "blur" | "hover" | "press" | "release" | "cancel", target: Entity | string, fn: (e: UiEvent) => void | boolean): () => void
members.doc: Listens to a widget event from one widget only (a "cancel" handler that returns true consumes ui_cancel, see above); `target` is the widget Entity or its entity id, e.g. ui.on("click", "play_button", () => scene.load("scenes/level1.scene.json")).

Gives keyboard / gamepad focus to a Button, Toggle, Slider, TextField or Interactable (null clears the focus) and sends ui.focus. Nothing takes focus by itself except a widget with autoFocus when none is focused, so call this when a menu opens. ui.focus(null) holds: an open Panel's autoFocus does not take the focus back until the next ui_up / ui_down / ui_left / ui_right press (that first press only wakes autoFocus, it does not also move the focus). Returns true when the widget took focus, and false (changing nothing) when it is a Button, Toggle, Slider or TextField with interactable false (or an Interactable with enabled false), so a screen that restores a remembered focus can fall back to another widget. Throws, saying why and what to do, when the entity cannot take focus at all (not a focusable widget, or inactive).

members.sig: speak(text: string, opts?: { interrupt?: boolean }): void
members.doc: Says `text` aloud with the system's text to speech (Windows SAPI, macOS/iOS AVSpeechSynthesizer, Android TextToSpeech, Linux speech-dispatcher, the browser's speechSynthesis), in the current language (i18n.language): the system voice for it when there is one. `interrupt` (default true) stops what is being said first; false queues the line after the ones before it. Speech is output only and never touches the simulation. Where the system has no speech (ui.speechAvailable is false) it does nothing and logs one warning per run. Headless runs and tests say nothing and record the line for game.spoken(). Pass an already localized string: ui.speak(i18n.t("menu.play")). Example: ui.on("focus", (e) => ui.speak(e.entity.get("Button").text)). Same as the ui.speak command.

members.sig: caption(text: string, seconds?: number, opts?: { key?: string; speaker?: string }): void
members.doc: Shows a subtitle line on the Captions component for `seconds` (default 3) of the game clock, for dialogue or hints that have no sound file; a sound's own subtitle is audio.play(path, { caption }). With `key` (a localization key) the line is the translation and follows a language change while it shows; `text` is then the fallback and may be "". `speaker` is a name drawn before the line. The newest Captions.maxLines lines show, the oldest drop first. Without a Captions entity the line is only tracked and the log says so once. Same as the ui.caption command. Example: ui.caption("Watch out!", 2, { speaker: "Mara" }).
Removes every caption now, also the ones of sounds that still play (the sounds are not stopped). Same as the ui.clear_captions command.
Stops what is being said and drops the queued lines. Does nothing when nothing is being said or the system has no speech. Same as the ui.stop_speaking command.

True when the system can speak. False on a Linux without speech-dispatcher (libspeechd.so.2) or an Android without a speech engine: hide your "read menus aloud" option then. Headless runs and tests report true because they record what would be said (game.spoken()).

members.sig: widgetAt(x: number, y: number): Entity | null
members.doc: The topmost visible widget at a screen point, in design pixels with y down (like ui.rectOf): a Button, Toggle, Slider, TextField, ScrollList, Interactable, Panel that draws something (a fully transparent Panel with no texture is skipped), or a TouchStick / TouchButton that is shown. Topmost is the highest `layer`, then the entity made last. It is null over empty space, over an inactive widget and where a ScrollList clips the widget away (a row scrolled out of view). It includes widgets with interactable false, so check Button.interactable for a click target. Reads the last layout: call it after game.step or ui.layout(). A screen-space widget wins over a world-space Interactable under the same point, which is looked up through the camera that draws at that point. Use it for a gamepad cursor and for "is the pointer over the UI" questions. Example: const w = ui.widgetAt(640, 360); if (w && w.has("Button")) console.log(w.id);

members.sig: setPointer(x: number, y: number, opts?: { down?: boolean }): void
members.doc: A virtual pointer for a gamepad cursor and for tests: from the next UI update (the next frame) the UI takes the pointer position and left button from here instead of from the mouse, so ui.hovered, press, a Slider drag, click and the wheel's target work as with the mouse. A click is `down: true` for a frame, then `down: false` while the pointer is still over the same widget. The real mouse is ignored until setPointer(null). Do not also bind the same button to ui_submit while a widget is focused: both would click. A scene load gives the pointer back to the mouse. x, y in design pixels, y down.
Gives the pointer back to the real mouse after a setPointer(x, y).

True when the pointer (the mouse, or the virtual one of setPointer) was over a visible widget or Panel at this frame's UI update (the UI runs before scripts, so it is current): the widgetAt(pointer) check. A game's own world click or camera zoom skips when it is true. A Panel that draws nothing (alpha 0, no texture) does not count.

True when the mouse wheel of this frame scrolled a ScrollList under the pointer, which has more content than it shows. input.mouse.wheel then reads 0 for the rest of the frame, so a camera that zooms with the wheel needs no check; a list that fits its content leaves the wheel alone. The UI runs before scripts, so the value is current in onUpdate.
The widget that has keyboard / gamepad focus, or null.
The widget under the mouse pointer (the top-most visible interactable one), or null. Check it in game code so a click meant for a button does not also shoot.

items.doc: Progress of scene.preload / assets.preload. Values change between frames only, never in the middle of your code. The files stay in memory through the first two scene loads after the job finishes (a load reads none of them from the disk); release() frees them earlier.

members.doc: How much of the work is done, 0..1: whole files read over the files to read (the scene file counts as one). Never goes down, 1 when done.
True once every file is read, or the job failed (then error says why).
Files read so far.
Bytes read so far.
Why the job failed (a file could not be read, the scene is not valid JSON), or an empty string.

members.sig: readonly promise: Promise<{ files: number; bytes: number }>
members.doc: Resolves with the totals when everything is read; rejects with an Error (message + hint) when the job fails or is released first.

Stops a job that is still running and drops the files nobody has read yet (they would be read from the disk again). Optional: the files leave memory by themselves after the second scene load that follows the job.

items.name: AssetsAPI
items.doc: Asset queries.

members.doc: Reads the files ahead of time like scene.preload does (models with their buffers and textures, images, audio, fonts, prefabs, materials), for assets a script will use later: the next read of each file, by the renderer or by audio, takes it from memory. A path that does not exist throws with a did-you-mean list; the list must not be empty. Example: assets.preload(["assets/boss.glb", "assets/boss_theme.ogg"]).promise.then(() => spawnBoss()).

members.sig: textureSize(path: string): { width: number; height: number }
members.doc: Pixel size of the texture file at the project-relative `path`, e.g. assets.textureSize("assets/hero.png"). This is the size a Sprite without `size` or `region` is drawn at and that entity.bounds() uses. A missing or unreadable file gives 32 x 32, the size of the missing-texture checker. Cached per file and modification time, so it is cheap to call every frame. Works headless (it reads the file, not the GPU texture). Throws for an empty or non-string path.

items.name: PlatformService
items.doc: A group of platform functions a backend may or may not offer; platform.has(service) tells. The functions of a missing service reject with code "unavailable". "http" is http.fetch: it is offered when the system's HTTP client can run (always in tests, which answer from game.platform.respond).

members.doc: The store's id of the player ("" when nobody is signed in).
The player's display name.
False when nobody is signed in: calls then reject with code "notSignedIn".

The catalog id of the product (as in factoria.json platform.products).
Only when purchased: pass it to purchases.finish() once the goods are delivered.
Only when purchased: the store's proof of purchase, for a server that wants to verify it.

members.doc: Unlocks an achievement; `newly` is false when it already was. An id the catalog does not declare throws at once with a suggestion.

members.doc: Reports progress from 0 to 1 toward an achievement; 1 unlocks it. Progress never goes down.

members.sig: list(): Promise<{ id: string; name: string; description: string; unlocked: boolean; progress: number }[]>
members.doc: The state of every achievement of the catalog, with its name and description in the current language (the catalog's nameKey / descriptionKey translated, else name / description; a store that answers its own texts wins).
Development only: locks every achievement again (the fake backend; real stores usually refuse).

items.name: PlatformStatsAPI
items.doc: Numbers the store keeps for the player (factoria.json platform.stats).

members.doc: The stat's value (0 when never set).
Sets the stat and resolves with the stored value. An int stat needs a whole number.

Resolves with the new value (an int stat needs a whole delta). The fake store (development, tests) adds on the value it holds when it serves the request, so two adds made in one frame both count. A real store gets a get() then a set(), which is not atomic.

items.name: PlatformLeaderboardsAPI
items.doc: Leaderboards of factoria.json platform.leaderboards. A board with "period": "daily" or "weekly" starts over with each calendar day or week of game.today(): submit and entries always address the current one (the fake keeps one per period; Steam makes one board per period, Game Center and Play Games use their own time scopes: docs/PLATFORM.md, "Leaderboard periods"; each store starts a period at its own time).

members.sig: submit(id: string, score: number, options?: { day?: string }): Promise<{ id: string; score: number; best: number; periodStart?: string; periodEnd?: string }>
members.doc: Submits a whole-number score (a time in milliseconds, not seconds); `best` is the player's best afterwards. The leaderboard's order decides what better means. `periodStart` and `periodEnd` (ISO 8601 UTC text) are there when the store says when the board's period runs. options.day: "YYYY-MM-DD" submits to the daily board of that day instead of today's (without it the board of the local date, game.today().iso; pass game.today().utc.iso to submit and entries alike for one board worldwide); only a daily board takes it, and Game Center and Play Games reject a day other than the local or UTC today with code "unsupported".

members.sig: entries(id: string, options?: { range?: "top" | "around" | "friends"; count?: number; day?: string }): Promise<PlatformLeaderboardEntry[] & { periodStart?: string; periodEnd?: string }>
members.doc: Reads entries: the best ("top", default), the ones around the player, or the player's friends; count 1..100 (default 10). For a daily or weekly board the array has `periodStart` and `periodEnd` (ISO 8601 UTC text) when the store says when the period runs. options.day: "YYYY-MM-DD" reads the daily board of that day, e.g. yesterday's (the same key submit wrote: the local date by default, game.today().utc.iso if the game submits with it; the fake and Steam keep every day, Game Center and Play Games reject a day other than the local or UTC today with code "unsupported").

items.doc: A guest connected through Steam's Remote Play Together, as the store describes the session.

members.doc: The session id Steam gave the guest's connection (the fake numbers them from 1). It identifies the session in the "disconnected" event too.
The guest's name on the store (Steam's persona name); "" when the store does not say.
The guest's account id on the store (a SteamID as decimal text); "" when unknown.
The name of the guest's device, as Steam reports it.
The kind of device the guest plays on: a phone or a tablet has no keyboard and a small screen, so a game may show bigger touch-free prompts.

members.sig: readonly resolution: { width: number; height: number } | null
members.doc: The guest's screen in pixels; null when Steam does not know it.

items.doc: The payload of platform.on("remotePlay").

members.doc: connected: a guest joined; disconnected: the guest left (the session is as it was when they were connected).

The guest's session. It says who is connected, not which pad is theirs: the guest's input arrives as one more gamepad (input.gamepad(i), game.on("gamepadConnected")), and the engine does not map a session to a pad index.

items.name: PlatformRemotePlayAPI
items.doc: Remote Play Together: friends who join the game through Steam and play on their own device. Offered by the Steam backend (check platform.has("remotePlay")); the fake backend simulates guests in tests (game.platform.remotePlayConnect). Steam shows each guest's controller to the game as one more gamepad, so a local multiplayer game already works with them; this API tells who is connected.

members.doc: The guests connected now (an empty array when nobody is). Guests already connected when the game starts are listed here but no "remotePlay" event announces them: read this list at the start. Rejects with code "unavailable" when the backend has no remotePlay service.

items.name: PlatformCloudAPI
items.doc: Cloud saves: small named values the store keeps for the player across devices.

members.sig: save(key: string, value: Json): Promise<{ key: string; bytes: number }>
members.doc: Stores any JSON value under a key (1-64 letters, digits, '_', '.', '-'). Stores limit how much a game may keep in the cloud, so save small things (settings, progress), not assets.
The stored value, or undefined when the key does not exist.
The stored keys.
Deletes a key.

members.sig: stat(key: string): Promise<{ exists: false } | { exists: true; size: number; modified: number | null }>
members.doc: Reads the size and modified time of a key without returning its text: { exists: false } for a key that is not there (not an error), else size (bytes of the saved JSON text) and modified (Unix seconds, a number you can compare, or null when the store keeps no time: Apple's iCloud key-value store). Steam answers the file's time, Google Play the snapshot's last modified time, the fake a counter that starts at 1767225600 and goes up one second with each save (game.platform.set({ cloudClock }) sets it). A store's time comes from the clock of the device that saved, which may be wrong: to decide which of two saves is newer, keep a revision counter inside the saved value and use `modified` only as a hint.

items.name: PlatformPurchasesAPI
items.doc: In-app purchases of factoria.json platform.products.

members.doc: Titles and prices as the store shows them, for the given catalog ids (all by default). Products the store does not know are left out.

Starts a purchase. Resolves also when the player cancels (status "cancelled"); rejects when the store failed (network, notAllowed...). Deliver the goods when status is "purchased", then call finish().

Tells the store the goods were delivered, once per transaction (consumables can be bought again only after this). Take transactionId from buy(), a "purchase" event or restore(). A transaction the game was not told about (or finished already) rejects with code "unknownId".

members.sig: restore(): Promise<{ productId: string; transactionId: string; receipt: string }[]>
members.doc: The non-consumables and subscriptions the player owns (a "Restore purchases" button).

items.name: PlatformOverlayAPI
items.doc: The store's own overlay (Steam overlay, Game Center dashboard).

members.doc: Opens a page of the overlay; `id` (an achievement, leaderboard or product of the catalog) goes to that entry where the store can. Pause the game on the "overlay" event while it is open.

items.name: PlatformPresenceAPI
items.doc: Rich presence: what friends see the player doing.

members.sig: set(text: string, data?: { [key: string]: string }): Promise<void>
members.doc: Sets the text ("In level 3"); "" clears it. `data` holds string values some stores use (Steam's rich presence keys).

items.name: PlatformConsent
items.doc: What the player answered to the consent sheets, from ads.consent().

members.doc: The GDPR (Google UMP) sheet: granted, denied, notRequired (the player is outside the regions that need it) or unknown (not asked yet).

The tracking permission (Apple's App Tracking Transparency): notRequired where the system has no such sheet (Android) and on iOS when platform.ads.trackingPrompt is off; otherwise the status of the sheet the ads plugin asks for after the consent form.
False when the player refused the GDPR consent: no ad may be requested then.

Whether the game must offer a way to change the ad choices (GDPR): required means the player has to find a "Privacy settings" button that calls platform.ads.privacyOptions(); notRequired where the consent sheet does not apply; unknown before the consent flow finished.

items.name: PlatformAdsAPI
items.doc: Advertising at the placements of factoria.json platform.ads.placements. Development runs and tests get a scripted test ad that draws nothing and ends at once (game.platform.ad() chooses how); a shipped Android game gets Google AdMob with the Google consent sheet (UMP) when it has the admob plugin (platform.add_backend admob), and any other shipped game rejects every call with code "unavailable" until a backend offers ads (check platform.has("ads")). Use platform.release to keep a development-only ad stub out of a shipped game. Children: factoria.json platform.ads.audience (docs/PLATFORM.md, "Children and consent").

members.doc: True when a rewarded ad is ready to show at the placement (false: no fill, or the player refused the consent). Use it to show or hide the "watch an ad" button. A placement the catalog does not declare throws at once with a suggestion.

members.sig: showRewarded(placement: string): Promise<{ rewarded: boolean; reason?: "closedEarly" | "noFill" | "consentRefused" }>
members.doc: Shows a rewarded ad and resolves when it ends. rewarded is true only when the player watched it to the end: give the reward then and only then. Otherwise reason says why: closedEarly (the player closed it), noFill (no ad to show), consentRefused (the player refused the consent). Rejects with code "network" or "unavailable" when the platform failed.
What the GDPR and tracking sheets answered, for the game's privacy screen.

Tells the ad network whether the player is under the age of consent (use 16, the highest age of consent in Europe). Call it after the game asked the player's age with a neutral screen (the menu kit's ageGate part does). The engine keeps the answer for the session and sends it with every ads request: AdMob then tags the requests as child-directed and under the age of consent, and the consent sheet is not shown to a child. With factoria.json platform.ads.audience "mixed" no ad is shown before this is called (available() is false, showRewarded() ends with reason "consentRefused"); with "children" every player counts as under age and setUnderAge(false) throws.

Opens the consent form where the player changes their ad choices. Show a "Privacy settings" button that calls it only when consent().privacyOptions is "required" (the menu kit's options screen does). Resolves when the form closes; shown is false when there was no form to open.
Who plays, from factoria.json platform.ads.audience (default "general").
The answer of setUnderAge() for this session: true or false; true in a "children" game; null while the game has not asked.

items.name: PlatformIntegrityAPI
items.doc: Integrity checks: the platform signs a statement that this is the genuine app on a genuine device, and the game's own server verifies it.

members.doc: Asks the platform for a signed integrity token. `challenge` is a nonce your server made: 16 to 500 characters of URL-safe Base64 (A-Z a-z 0-9 - _ =), e.g. 16 or more random bytes. Send the token to your server, which must verify it with the store's server API and check the challenge inside the decoded token (a token without a fresh challenge can be replayed); never trust the client's word. A bad challenge throws at once. Offered by some stores only (Google Play): check platform.has("integrity") and let the game work without it; otherwise the Promise rejects with code "unavailable".

items.name: PlatformAPI
items.doc: Store and platform services behind one API: achievements, stats, leaderboards, cloud saves, purchases, overlay, presence, integrity, ads, Remote Play guests. factoria.json "platform" declares the ids; a store plugin (Steam, Apple) answers in a shipped game, a deterministic fake in development, tests and the MCP server. Every function returns a Promise; a mistake in the call (an undeclared id, a wrong type) throws at once with a suggestion, a store failure rejects with an Error that has `code` ("unavailable", "notSignedIn", "notAllowed", "unknownId", "network" or "failed") and `hint`. Answers that arrive later settle at the start of the next frame. See docs/PLATFORM.md.

members.doc: Which backend answers: "fake" (development, tests), "none" (no store: every call rejects with "unavailable"), or the plugin's backend name ("steam", "apple").
Which backend answers platform.ads: an ads plugin ("admob"), the store backend when it offers ads itself ("fake"), or "none" when nothing offers ads.

True when the backend offers the service, e.g. if (platform.has("leaderboards")) hide the button otherwise. An unknown service throws with a suggestion. platform.has("http") tells whether http.fetch can run: false when this computer has no HTTP client (a Linux without libcurl).
The last known player (from signIn() and "player" events).
Signs the player in (or reads who is signed in). Always allowed, even when nobody is.

Listens to purchases that did not come from a buy() call: Ask to Buy approved, an unfinished transaction from an earlier run, a purchase made in the store. Deliver the goods and call purchases.finish(e.transactionId). Events that arrive while nobody listens are kept (up to 100) and delivered to the first listener. Returns the function that stops listening; listeners end with the scene, like ui.on.

members.sig: on(event: "overlay", fn: (e: { open: boolean }) => void): () => void
members.doc: The store's overlay opened or closed: pause the game while it is open.
The signed-in player changed.
A guest joined or left through Remote Play Together ({ status, session }). Only a backend with the "remotePlay" service (Steam; the fake in tests) sends it.
True in a shipped game, false in development runs (`factoria run`, the editor), tests and the MCP server. Use it to leave out what is only for development, such as a test-ad stub or a cheat button.

items.name: HttpFetchOptions
items.doc: The options of http.fetch. Every field is optional.

members.doc: The HTTP method, "GET" by default (lower case works too). Another method throws with a suggestion. PATCH works on every platform (Android sends it as POST with X-HTTP-Method-Override).

Request headers: at most 32, string values, no duplicates (names ignore case). Host, Content-Length, Connection, Transfer-Encoding, Upgrade, Expect, TE, Trailer, Keep-Alive, Proxy-* and Sec-* are set by the system and throw.
The request body, at most 1 MB, not for GET or HEAD. A string is sent as it is; an object or array is sent as JSON, with Content-Type application/json unless you set a content type yourself.
Seconds to wait for the whole request, above 0 and at most 120. Default 15. A request that takes longer rejects with code "network".

items.name: HttpResponse
items.doc: What http.fetch resolves with: the server's answer, whatever its status. Immutable.

members.doc: The HTTP status code: 200, 404, 500...
True for a status from 200 to 299.
The response headers with lower-case names; a header the server sent twice is joined with ", ".
The body as text (UTF-8; bytes that are not valid UTF-8 become U+FFFD). At most 4 MB: a bigger answer rejects with code "network".
The body parsed as JSON. Throws an Error that shows the start of the body when it is not JSON; check ok and the content-type header first when the server may answer an error page.

items.name: HttpAPI
items.doc: HTTP requests to the hosts the game declares in factoria.json "network" (docs/NETWORKING.md): a leaderboard server, a news feed, a daily seed. Only https:// URLs (plain http:// only to localhost, for development); a host that is not declared throws at once. Works the same on Windows, macOS, iOS, Linux, Android and the web; in tests and headless runs the fake answers what game.platform.respond scripted and never touches the network. Example: `const r = await http.fetch("https://api.example.com/scores"); if (r.ok) show(r.json());`.

members.doc: Sends one request. Resolves with the server's answer even for 404 or 500 (look at response.ok); rejects with an Error that has `code` ("network": no connection, DNS, TLS, timeout, too big an answer; "unavailable": no HTTP client on this computer) and `hint`. A mistake in the call (a host factoria.json "network" does not declare, a http:// URL, a bad header or body) throws at once with what to change. Redirects are followed, to https only, at most 5. The answer settles at the start of an engine frame, maybe long after your code ran: a script that awaits it must check that its scene is still the current one (scene.current, entity.alive) before it uses the answer. Example: `const r = await http.fetch(url, { method: "POST", body: { name, score } });`.

items.name: AnalyticsAPI
items.doc: Usage analytics with consent (docs/ANALYTICS.md). analytics.event(name, props) queues small anonymous events and sends them in batches to the endpoint of factoria.json "analytics" through http.fetch, but only after the player said yes with analytics.setConsent(true): before that nothing is kept or sent, and a refusal forgets what waited. A batch goes out when `batch` events wait, when the oldest waited `flushSeconds`, when the app is suspended and when the game quits (the quit waits up to 3 seconds for the request). A network failure keeps the events and retries later; a 4xx answer drops them. Without the section, event(), flush() and setConsent() throw with what to add; check `configured` in code shared between games. Say what is sent in your privacy policy (docs/LEGAL.md). Example: `if (analytics.consent() === "unknown") askPlayer(); analytics.event("level_done", { level: 3, won: true });`.

members.doc: True when factoria.json has an "analytics" section with an endpoint.

The player's answer, kept between runs; "unknown" when not asked yet (event() then keeps nothing). With factoria.json analytics.consentFromAds, an unanswered question follows the ad consent (granted when the GDPR consent is granted and tracking is authorized or not required); the player's own answer always wins.
Records the player's answer (kept between runs). false forgets every event waiting to be sent. Throws when the game has no analytics section or yes is not a boolean.

members.sig: event(name: string, props?: Record<string, string | number | boolean | null>): boolean
members.doc: Queues one event and returns true; returns false (keeping nothing) when the player has not said yes. The name starts with a letter and uses letters, digits, "_", "." and "-" (at most 64 characters). props is a flat object of strings, numbers, booleans or null: at most 20 props, texts of at most 200 characters (never what the player typed), at most 2048 characters of props as JSON. A mistake throws with the limit (analytics.limits). The time of the event is engine seconds since the run started.

Sends what waits now, in one request of at most 100 events. Resolves { sent, ok }; a failure is ok: false and keeps the events for a retry. Rejects only for a mistake of the call (no analytics section). The answer settles at the start of an engine frame, maybe after the scene changed.
The state, for debugging: queue length, failures, retry time, consent.
The limits event() checks.

items.name: RemoteConfigAPI
items.doc: Values the game reads from a server (docs/ANALYTICS.md): balance numbers, an event flag, a message. The JSON object at factoria.json "remoteConfig".url is fetched once, at the first use, through http.fetch, and its last good answer is cached in storage, so an offline player gets the values of the last run and a first-time offline player gets the defaults. get(key, fallback) always works: with no section, no connection or a value of the wrong type it returns fallback. A bad answer (not a JSON object, over 64 KB or 500 keys, a 4xx or 5xx status) is ignored as a whole, never half applied. Example: `const speed = remoteConfig.get("enemySpeed", 1.5);`. A script that awaits ready() or refresh() must check that its scene is still the current one (scene.current) before it uses the answer.

members.doc: True when factoria.json has a "remoteConfig" section with a url.

members.sig: get<T extends Json>(key: string, fallback: T): T
members.doc: The server's value of key; else the cached one; else fallback. A value whose type differs from the fallback's (a text where you expect a number) counts as missing. Returns a copy: changing it changes nothing. The first call starts the fetch.
Where the values come from now: this run's fetch, the cache of an earlier run, or only the defaults.
Resolves with source() when the first fetch ended or timeoutSeconds (engine seconds, default 3) passed. Never rejects: a game waits for it at its loading screen and plays on with whatever it has.
Fetches again; resolves with source() when the answer (or the failure) arrived.

members.doc: The language now in use.
The language before.

items.name: I18nAPI
items.doc: Localization: the strings of locales/<language>.json in the player's language. factoria.json "localization" lists the languages; without it the game is not localized (t(key) returns the key, languages is []). Components with a `key` field (Text, Button, Toggle, Slider, TextField) are translated by the engine; use t() for text a script builds itself. The chosen language is not saved between runs: keep it with `storage` and call setLanguage at start. See docs/LOCALIZATION.md.

members.sig: t(key: string, args?: { count?: number; gender?: string; [name: string]: unknown }): string
members.doc: The text of `key` in the current language, else in its base language ("pt" for "pt-BR"), else in the default language. `{name}` placeholders are filled from args; a plural entry is chosen by args.count with the language's CLDR rules; a select entry (forms f, m, n, other) by args.gender (see gender()), "other" when the gender or the form is missing. A key that no table has returns the key itself and warns once in the log; it never throws for a missing key. A key that is not a string or args that is not an object throws.

members.sig: number(value: number, options?: { decimals?: number }): string
members.doc: `value` written the way the current language writes numbers: decimal and group separators and digits from the engine's table (en "1,234.5", es "1234,5" and "12.345,5", de "1.234,5", fr "1 234,5" with a narrow no-break space, ar Arabic-Indic digits "١٬٢٣٤٫٥"). `decimals` (0 to 9) fixes the digits after the separator; without it the number keeps the digits it has. A language the table does not know writes like English; a game without localization is English. Same as the `{v:number:1}` placeholder of a string table. Throws for a value that is not a number or decimals out of range.

members.sig: duration(seconds: number, options?: { decimals?: number }): string
members.doc: `seconds` as a time in the current language: "1:23.4" for 83.4 (minutes:seconds), "1:02:03.4" from one hour on. `decimals` (0 to 3, default 1) are the digits of the second; the decimal separator and the digits follow the language (es "1:23,4", ar "١:٢٣٫٤"). Rounded as a whole, so 59.96 is "1:00.0". Same as the `{t:duration}` placeholder of a string table.
True when a table of the current language's fallback chain has `key`, so a real string can be told from the key returned for a missing one.

The grammatical gender of the string `key` in the current language ("f" feminine, "m" masculine, "n" neuter), from a table entry written {"text": "Ligera", "gender": "f"}; "" when the string has none or no table has the key. Pass it as args.gender to a select entry (an object with forms f, m, n and other) to get the article or adjective that agrees: i18n.t("ship.the", { name: i18n.t("ship.light"), gender: i18n.gender("ship.light") }) is "la Ligera" in Spanish. Throws for a key that is not a string. See docs/LOCALIZATION.md, "Gender".
The current language (one of `languages`; "" when the game has no localization).

Switches now: every Text and widget with a `key` is rewritten at once and the "change" listeners run. Accepts the tag as in factoria.json or close to it ("pt_br", "es-MX" -> "es"). An unknown language throws with a "did you mean" and the languages the game has. Not saved: a game keeps the player's choice with `storage` and calls this at start.
The game's languages, as in factoria.json localization.languages.
factoria.json localization.defaultLanguage: the language of the text written in scenes and the last fallback.

The writing direction of the current language: "rtl" for Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, Urdu and the other right-to-left languages, else "ltr" (also when the game has no localization). Text align "start"/"end" and Panel direction "auto" follow it by themselves; read it to mirror what they do not reach, such as an anchor or a pivot (docs/LOCALIZATION.md, section 6).
The player's system languages, best first (BCP 47 tags such as "es-MX"). Empty in headless runs and tests: the start language does not depend on the machine there.
The language's own name for a language menu ("Español"): the "$name" of its table, else the tag.
Runs fn after every language switch (setLanguage or the i18n.set_language command). Returns the function that stops listening; listeners end with the scene, like ui.on, so register in onStart.

items.name: AnimatorAPI
items.doc: Plays the clips of an entity with an Animator component (entity.animator): the animations of a skinned glTF, or the keyframed 2D clips (`*.anim.json`) listed in the Animator's `clips`. The engine advances it in the fixed step, so animation, its events and state machine transitions are deterministic. Example: `hero.animator.set("speed", 3)`; `hero.animator.on("footstep", () => audio.play("assets/step.wav"))`.

members.doc: Starts a clip (a glTF animation name or a key of the Animator's `clips`, see `clips`), cross-fading from the current pose over `fadeSeconds` (default: the component's `fade`; 0 cuts). Playing the clip that already plays does not restart it. Throws with the clip names when it does not exist.
Pauses and returns to the bind pose (the model as exported).

members.sig: set(name: string, value: number | boolean): void
members.doc: Sets a state machine parameter declared in the Animator's `params`. The transitions read it on the next step.
Current value of a state machine parameter.
Makes the parameter `name` true for the next step only (one-shot input like "jump" or "hurt"). It does not need to be declared.
Names of the animation clips: those of the model, or the keys of the Animator's `clips` for 2D clip files.
Length of a clip in seconds (the `duration` of the file for a 2D clip).

2D clips only: poses the entity and its children at `time` seconds into `clip` without playing (time is clamped to the clip). The Animator stays paused on that pose; use it for previews, thumbnails and tests. Throws with the clip names when the clip does not exist, or with the file and JSON pointer when a track does not fit the entity.

2D clips only: sets the weight (0..1) of the layer called `layer` in the Animator's `layers`. At 0 the layer is not playing; it starts from its first pose when the weight rises. Throws with the layer names when there is no such layer.

members.sig: playLayer(layer: string, clip: string, fadeSeconds?: number): void
members.doc: 2D clips only: makes the layer called `layer` play `clip` (a key of `clips`), cross-fading over `fadeSeconds` (default: the component's `fade`). A layer that runs its own `states` cannot be driven this way.

members.sig: on(event: string, fn: (data: { id: string; clip?: string; time?: number; state?: string }, source: Entity | null) => void): () => void
members.doc: Listens to a game event of THIS entity's animator: a clip event from the Animator's `events`, a state's `onEnter` name, or "anim.finished". Returns the unsubscribe function. world.on(name, fn) hears every entity.
State machine: the current state.
The clip playing now. Assigning switches clips with the component's `fade`.
Seconds into the current clip. Assigning seeks (no events fire for the jump).
Playback speed multiplier.
Start over at the end of the clip. false stops on the last pose and sends "anim.finished".
false pauses, true resumes.
The Animator component view (model, params, states, transitions, events...).

items.name: SpriteAnimatorAPI
items.doc: Plays the named clips of a sprite sheet on an entity with a Sprite and a SpriteAnimator (entity.spriteAnimator). The clips are those of the `sheet` entry of the sprite's texture in assets.json (assets.animate_svg, assets.bake_sheet, assets.slice_sheet and the Aseprite import write it). The renderer steps the animation with the frame time, so it runs with a renderer (a headless run has one when a GPU is found). Example: `fx.spriteAnimator.play("pop"); fx.spriteAnimator.on("clipEnded", () => fx.destroy());`.

members.doc: Starts the clip `clip` of the texture's sheet from its first frame and plays it. Asking for the clip that already plays (and has not ended) does nothing unless `restart` is true, so it may be called every frame. Throws with the clip names (and a "did you mean") when the sheet has no such clip.
Pauses on the current frame.
Continues after stop().
Names of the clips of the sprite texture's sheet. Throws when the texture has no sheet entry.

members.sig: clipInfo(clip: string): { name: string; firstFrame: number; lastFrame: number; frames: number; fps: number; loop: boolean; pivot?: [number, number] }
members.doc: The sheet entry of one clip (pivot from the TOP-left of the frame, as stored). Throws with the clip names when it does not exist.

members.sig: on(event: "clipEnded", fn: (data: { id: string; clip: string }, source: Entity | null) => void): () => void
members.doc: Listens to the game event of THIS entity's animator: "clipEnded", sent once when a clip that does not loop (loop false in the sheet or the component) reaches its end. Returns the unsubscribe function. world.on("clipEnded", fn) hears every entity.
The clip playing now (SpriteAnimator.clip). Assigning another name restarts the animation.
Order of the frames.
Index in the sheet's grid (row-major from the top-left) of the frame shown.
Seconds into the current clip. Assigning seeks (set playing to true to run a finished clip again).
false pauses, true resumes.
True after a clip that does not loop reached its end.
The SpriteAnimator component view (columns, rows, firstFrame, lastFrame, fps, loop, clip, mode, sheetPivot...).

items.name: TilemapAPI
items.doc: Reads and writes single tiles of a Tilemap (entity.tilemap) and converts between cells and world points (cellAt, cellToWorld) for square and isometric maps. A write changes one element of `tiles` in place: the array is not copied to the script and back, the renderer reads the tiles directly and 2D physics rebuilds only the colliders of the cells you changed, so digging or opening a door every frame is cheap. Example: `map.tilemap.setTile(12, 7, -1)` empties a cell; `if (map.tilemap.getTile(x, y) === 3) ...`.

members.doc: The tile value at column x, row y (0-based, row 0 = TOP row): the tile index plus flip/rotate flag bits, -1 when empty or outside the map. Mask with `& 0xFFFFFFF` for the plain index.

members.sig: setTile(x: number, y: number, tile: number): void
members.doc: Writes the tile at column x, row y: a tileset index (plus optional flip flags) or -1 to empty it. Throws an Error that names the map size when the cell is outside the map or the value is not a tile. 2D collision follows on the next physics step.

members.sig: cellAt(point: Vec2Like): { col: number; row: number } | null
members.doc: The cell under a WORLD point, by the entity's transform and the map's `projection` (the square for "orthogonal", the diamond for "isometric"); null when the point is outside the map. To pick the cell under the mouse pass `camera.screenToWorld(input.mouse.position)`. `cellToWorld(col, row)` is the inverse for the centre of a cell. Example: `const c = ground.tilemap.cellAt(camera.screenToWorld(input.mouse.position)); if (c) ground.tilemap.setTile(c.col, c.row, 3)`.

The WORLD position of the centre of cell (col, row) (0-based, row 0 = TOP row), by the entity's transform and the map's `projection`: the middle of the square, or of the diamond. The cell may lie outside the map. `cellAt(cellToWorld(c, r))` is `{ col: c, row: r }` for a cell inside the map.
Map width in tiles.
Map height in tiles (rows).
The Tilemap component view.

items.doc: Controls a Video component (entity.video): an .mpg drawn in the entity's UI rectangle. The engine advances it in the fixed step from the game clock, so it pauses with the game and a headless run is deterministic. Example: `intro.video.on("ended", () => scene.load("scenes/menu.scene.json"))`; `intro.video.seek(10)`.

members.doc: Plays, or resumes after pause(). After the end it starts over from the first picture.
Stops advancing and keeps the picture; the sound goes silent.
Pauses and returns to the first picture.
Jumps to `seconds` (clamped to the length) and shows the picture there. Keeps playing if it was playing; no "ended" event comes from a seek.

members.sig: on(event: "ended", fn: (data: { id: string; path: string }, source: Entity | null) => void): () => void
members.doc: Listens to the "ended" event of THIS entity's video: a video that does not loop reached its end (once per play). Returns the unsubscribe function. world.on("video.ended", fn) hears every Video.
Seconds into the video.
Length in seconds; 0 until the file is open (the first fixed step after the scene loads).
True while it advances.
True after it reached its end, until a seek or play() starts it again.
Wrap to the first picture at the end instead of ending.
Loudness of the sound, 0..1.

items.doc: Hooks of bt.action.

members.doc: Runs when the action starts (the first tick it is reached, or after it finished or was interrupted).
Runs when the action returns SUCCESS or FAILURE, or with "aborted" when a tick did not reach it (a selector chose an earlier child) or the tree was reset.

items.name: BtTree
items.doc: A behaviour tree with its own memory per node: ten enemies can each run a Tree built from the same node description.

members.doc: The root node.
The object every condition and action receives.
Seconds the tree has run: the sum of the dt it was ticked with.
Result of the last tick.
Runs the tree one step; call it once per frame with the dt of onUpdate. A node that was not ticked on the previous tick starts fresh (a sequence goes back to its first child, a wait to zero).
Forgets what every node remembers (running actions get onExit with "aborted").

items.name: BtAPI
items.doc: Behaviour trees in plain JS, ticked by your script with a dt you pass (deterministic). Example: const tree = new bt.Tree(bt.selector(bt.sequence(bt.condition((b) => b.sees), bt.action((b, dt) => { b.chase(dt); return bt.RUNNING; })), bt.action((b, dt) => { b.wander(dt); return bt.RUNNING; })), enemy); in onUpdate(dt): tree.tick(dt).

members.doc: Status: the node finished well.
Status: the node failed or its condition was false.
Status: the node needs more ticks.

members.sig: readonly Tree: new (root: BtNode, blackboard?: any) => BtTree
members.doc: Creates a tree for one agent.
Ticks the children in order: FAILURE as soon as one fails, RUNNING while one runs (the next tick resumes at that child without asking the earlier conditions again), SUCCESS when all succeeded.
Ticks the children in order from the FIRST one every tick, so a more important child can interrupt a running one; returns the first result that is not FAILURE.

Ticks the children in order every tick (the options object is optional: bt.parallel(a, b) is succeed "all"). FAILURE as soon as one child fails; with succeed "all" (default) SUCCESS once every child has succeeded (a child that succeeded is not ticked again meanwhile), with "any" SUCCESS at the first success; otherwise RUNNING. When it finishes, children still running are stopped (an action gets onExit(bb, "aborted")). No children: SUCCESS for "all", FAILURE for "any".
Same as parallel({ succeed: "all" }, ...children): all children at once, FAILURE at the first failure, SUCCESS when all succeeded.
Truthy = SUCCESS, falsy = FAILURE. Never RUNNING.

members.sig: action(fn: (blackboard: any, dt: number, tree: BtTree) => BtStatus, hooks?: BtActionHooks): BtNode
members.doc: Does something and returns bt.SUCCESS, bt.FAILURE or bt.RUNNING (anything else throws).
RUNNING for that many seconds of tick dt, then SUCCESS. Starts over when it was not ticked on the previous tick.
Ticks the child; once it finishes (SUCCESS or FAILURE) the node FAILS for `seconds` without ticking it. For an attack that must not repeat at once.

Runs the child again each time it succeeds. Returns RUNNING while it repeats, FAILURE as soon as the child fails, and with `times` (a whole number >= 1) SUCCESS after that many successes; without `times` it repeats forever. One run of the child per tick: the next run starts on the NEXT tick, so a child that succeeds at once cannot loop forever inside one tick.
Swaps SUCCESS and FAILURE; RUNNING stays.
SUCCESS whenever the child finishes, either way.

members.doc: Seconds per play (default 1).
Seconds to wait before it starts (default 0).
Easing (default "linear"). inOut easings play the in curve for the first half and its mirror image for the second.
Extra plays after the first (0 = once, Infinity = forever).
Every second play runs backwards.
Start values instead of the current ones, same shape as the end values: { x: 0 }. For tween(from, to, ...) the start is the first argument.
Called once when the delay is over and it starts moving (start values are read here).
Called after every update. `value` is the eased progress (can overshoot with back/elastic); for tween(from, to) it is the current number.
Called when the last play ends (never for a cancelled tween).

items.name: Tween
items.doc: A running tween, returned by tween(). Driven by the game clock: pauses with time.scale = 0 and while the game is paused (game.pause: it moves only with game.step), identical in headless runs.

members.doc: false once it completed or was cancelled.
0..1 over all plays (after the delay).

Resolves true when it completes and false when YOU cancel it (cancel(), cancelTweens). It stays pending forever, so the code awaiting it never resumes, when the tween is dropped: its target entity was destroyed, the Behaviour that started it with this.tween() was destroyed, or the scene was reloaded or unloaded. That makes `await tween(...).finished; entity.position = ...` safe without an alive check (a dropped tween cannot throw "entity was destroyed" into your code). Do not await it in a place that must always continue (Promise.all of several tweens); use onComplete or poll `active` there.
Stops it where it is (values stay as they are) and cancels the tweens chained after it.
Freezes it.
Continues after pause().

Jumps to `seconds` after the tween was created (the delay counts; past the end it completes) and applies the values there at once, also while it is paused: scrub an animation to a given time to inspect it. Backwards works while the tween is active. Throws on a tween that is complete or cancelled.
Adds a completion callback.

members.sig: next(target: object, props: object, options?: TweenOptions): Tween
members.doc: Starts another tween when this one completes (chain): `tween(a, {x: 1}).next(a, {y: 1}).next(b, {a: 0})`. Returns the NEW tween. Cancelling this one cancels the chain.

items.sig: didYouMean(word: string, choices: readonly string[]): string
items.doc: The choice closest to `word` (case-insensitive edit distance, accepted when within about a third of the word's length, at least 2), or "" when none is near. For errors that teach: `const near = didYouMean(id, goodIds); throw new ToolError(`unknown good '${id}'`, near ? `Did you mean '${near}'?` : "")`. Example: didYouMean("woood", ["wood", "stone"]) is "wood".

items.sig: tween(target: object, props: { [property: string]: number | string | readonly number[] | { [channel: string]: number } }, options?: TweenOptions): Tween
items.doc: Moves numbers, vectors and colors of `target` to the end values in `props` over time. Targets: a component view (`tween(sprite, {color: "#ff0000"})`), a vector (`tween(entity.position, {y: 5})`), a color, or a plain object. A vector end value is [x, y, z], {x, y, z} or a Vec; a color is "#rrggbb", [r, g, b, a] or {r, g, b, a}. Start values are read when the delay ends. Driven by the game clock (fixed step, time.scale), never by the wall clock. Example: `await tween(entity.position, {y: 3}, {duration: 0.5, ease: "backOut"}).finished`.

items.doc: The fake store, for tests: script what it answers, send it events, look at what it holds. Each test file starts with a fresh one; the real backends are never touched by tests. Backed by the platform.* commands. See docs/PLATFORM.md.

members.sig: respond(method: string, answer: Json, times?: number): void
members.doc: Queues the next answer(s) of a platform method (first in, first out, one per request). answer is { error: "network", message?, hint? } to reject, { result: value } to resolve with exactly that value, or any other object, which is merged into the default result: game.platform.respond("purchases.buy", { status: "cancelled" }). An unknown method throws with a suggestion. For "http.fetch" there is no default answer: a request nobody scripted rejects with code "network", so a test never depends on a server. Script it with { status: 200, json: { ... } } (json becomes the text, with a content-type header), { status: 404, text: "not found", headers: { "Retry-After": "5" } }, or { error: "network" } for an offline player; status 200, no headers and an empty text fill what you leave out. See docs/NETWORKING.md.
Sends an event as the store would; platform.on listeners get it at the next game.step(). A purchased "purchase" also records an unfinished transaction.

Takes a purchase back, as a refund does: restore() no longer lists the product, its unfinished transaction is dropped and platform.on("purchase") listeners get { status: "revoked", productId, transactionId, receipt } at the next game.step(). Throws when the player owns no such product, listing the owned ones.

members.sig: ad(outcome: "watched" | "closedEarly" | "noFill" | "consentRefused", options?: { gdpr?: "granted" | "denied" | "notRequired" | "unknown"; tracking?: "authorized" | "denied" | "notDetermined" | "restricted" | "notRequired"; privacyOptions?: "required" | "notRequired" | "unknown" }): void
members.doc: How the fake's test ad ends from now on: watched to the end (the default: rewarded), closedEarly (not rewarded), noFill (no ad: ads.available() is false) or consentRefused (also answers denied in ads.consent()). options.gdpr, options.tracking and options.privacyOptions set what ads.consent() answers (with privacyOptions "required", platform.ads.privacyOptions() counts a form shown); a denied gdpr stops every ad. reset() restores the defaults. state().fake.ads counts the ads shown and rewarded.

members.sig: remotePlayConnect(info?: { guestName?: string; guestId?: string; deviceName?: string; formFactor?: "unknown" | "phone" | "tablet" | "computer" | "tv" | "vr"; resolution?: { width: number; height: number } }): PlatformRemotePlaySession
members.doc: A guest joins Remote Play Together: platform.remotePlay.sessions() lists the session and platform.on("remotePlay") listeners get { status: "connected", session } at the next game.step(). What info leaves out is made up ("Guest 1", "fake-guest-1", "Fake device", "computer", 1920 x 1080); the sessions are numbered from 1. Returns the session. The guest's input is not simulated: drive the pad they would use with game.gamepad(i). An unknown field or form factor throws with a suggestion.

The guest with that session id leaves: sessions() no longer lists it and listeners get { status: "disconnected", session } at the next game.step(). Throws, listing the connected ids, when no guest has that id.
Fresh fake: nothing unlocked, bought or saved, no scripted answers, signed in, no Remote Play guests.

members.sig: set(options: { signedIn?: boolean; delayFrames?: number; backend?: "fake" | "none"; cloudClock?: number }): void
members.doc: An unknown option throws with a "did you mean". backend "none" makes the fake behave as the none backend, the case of an exported game without a store plugin (platform.has false for every service, every call rejects "unavailable", signIn answers signed out) until platform.reset(). signedIn false rejects every call but signIn() with "notSignedIn"; delayFrames n holds each answer for n frames (0 = answered at once), so a test can check a "waiting" state and game.step(n) to get the answer. cloudClock n (Unix seconds) is the modified time the next cloud.save gets, which cloud.stat() reports: it starts at 1767225600 (2026-01-01T00:00:00Z) and goes up one second with each save, so saves are ordered without the wall clock.

What the platform holds: { backend, services, player, catalog, pending, fake: { achievements, stats, leaderboards, cloud, cloudModified, remotePlay, owned, unfinished, presence, scripted, calls... } }.
Every request the game made, oldest first (the request log of state().fake.calls).

Same as the script `game.focused`.

members.sig: setDate(iso: string, options?: { utcOffsetMinutes?: number }): void
members.doc: Sets the date game.today() answers, "YYYY-MM-DD" or with a time "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM[:SS]" (midnight without one), until the test ends (the next test starts from the run's date again). options.utcOffsetMinutes sets the time zone (minutes east of UTC; the current one is kept otherwise), which decides game.today().utc. Moving to another local day sends "dayChanged" to the game.on listeners once, so a test crosses midnight with game.setDate("2026-10-23T23:59:59") then game.setDate("2026-10-24T00:00:01"). An impossible date or time throws with what is wrong and how to fix it. Example: game.setDate("2026-10-23"); expect(game.today().weekday).toBe(5).

The player clicks the window's close button (Cmd+Q, Alt+F4): the game.on("quit") handlers run at once. Returns false when one called event.cancel() (the game goes on), true otherwise: game.quitRequested is then true. Example: expect(game.closeWindow()).toBe(false).

The app goes to the background, as on a phone: the game.on("suspend") handlers run at once and, with pauseOnSuspend (the default), the game and the music freeze (game.paused is true) unless a handler paused it itself. Every test starts running.
The app comes back: undoes the freeze suspend() made (a pause the game made itself stays) and runs the game.on("resume") handlers.
The window gains the focus: game.focused becomes true and the game.on("focus") handlers run. Does nothing when it already had it.
The window loses the focus: game.focused becomes false and the game.on("blur") handlers run. Does not pause anything (a window that lost the focus keeps running).

Loads a scene immediately (reseeds the RNG). Behaviours are constructed right away (game.find(id).behaviour works); onStart runs on the first step(). `props` is what the scene reads with game.sceneProps(); without it the new scene has {}.

Files the engine has read from the disk since the run started. Read it twice and compare to prove that something read nothing: const before = game.fileReads(); scene.load(...); game.step(); expect(game.fileReads()).toBe(before). A file read ahead by scene.preload / assets.preload counts when it is preloaded, not when it is used.
Simulates frames at the fixed rate.
Holds an action down until release().

Taps what a player would press for the action: its first key binding (a chord included), else its first gamepad button, held for one frame and released over the next. The UI and every other action on that key or button see it too: game.tap("ui_submit") presses the focused Button or Toggle, and game.tap("interact") does what Space does when Space is also ui_submit. An action with no key or button binding (a stick, the mouse, none) is held as the action itself, which only readers of that action see.

Presses a key, steps one frame, releases it and steps one frame (like tap() for an action). A chord works too: tapKey("Ctrl+Z") holds Ctrl while Z is tapped. A TextField reads Enter itself, not an action, so game.tapKey("Enter") submits the focused field (ui.submit {id, value}).

Presses and HOLDS a key until keyUp: a key name ("Z", "LeftShift") or a modifier ("Ctrl", "Shift", "Alt", "Super": the left key), which is how a test holds Shift for a Shift+click: keyDown("Shift"); click(pos); keyUp("Shift").
Releases a key pressed with keyDown; takes the same names, modifiers included.
Types text as the keyboard would: input.text returns it until the next step(). Control characters are skipped, as the real keyboard does; press Enter and Backspace with keyDown()/keyUp() or tap().

Drags a Slider to `value` as a player would: clamped to [min, max], snapped to step, the slider takes focus and ui.change {id, value} is sent when the number changed (ui.on listeners get it at the next step()). Writing Slider.value from a script sends nothing; this does. Works on an Interactable of kind "slider" too. Throws when the entity is no slider, or is inactive or not interactable (enabled false for an Interactable).
Presses the system Back button of Android. The input.onBack handlers run at the next step(); when none consumes it the game asks to quit (game.quitRequested in game.state()).

members.sig: setSafeArea(insets: { left?: number; top?: number; right?: number; bottom?: number } | "none" | "phone-portrait" | "phone-landscape"): void
members.doc: Pretends the device has a notch, rounded corners or system bars: insets in design pixels from each edge (0 for those left out), or the profile of a typical phone. screen.safeArea, screen.insets and the items with `safeArea: true` follow at once (take a step() before checking layout of UI widgets). A negative or non-number inset throws. Reset to "none" before every test.

members.sig: setDevice(overrides: { formFactor?: "desktop" | "phone" | "tablet"; gpuBackend?: string; memoryGB?: number; tier?: "low" | "medium" | "high"; steamDeck?: boolean; handheld?: boolean }): void
members.doc: Pretends the game runs on another device: game.device follows at once (window.supports too, for the window features). Fields left out keep the headless values { formFactor: "desktop", gpuBackend: "headless", memoryGB: 8, tier: "high", steamDeck: false, handheld: false }, except handheld, which is true when you set steamDeck: true or a phone or tablet formFactor (and nothing else says it is not). For a Steam Deck: game.setDevice({ steamDeck: true }). An unknown field (with a suggestion) or a bad value throws. Reset before every test. Example: game.setDevice({ formFactor: "phone", tier: "low" }).

members.sig: renderStats(): { drawCalls: number; sprites: number; shapes: number; textGlyphs: number; particles: number; meshes: number; meshesCulled: number; meshBatches: number; triangles: number; views: number; shadowCasters: number; lights: number; lightsDropped: number; lights2d: number; lights2dDropped: number; lights2dShadowed: number; materials: number; materialFallbacks: string[]; textureMB: number; width: number; height: number; renderScale: number }
members.doc: What the renderer drew in the picture now, drawing a frame first when none has been drawn since the last change (a headless test may not have drawn one; game.state().renderStats stays zero until a frame is drawn). triangles and lights (the 3D lights) count the main pass, lights2d the Light2D lights shading 2D visuals (at most 256: directional first, then the point lights that reach the camera view; lights2dDropped are the ones left out; lights2dShadowed the ones given a shadow, castShadows, at most 32), shadowCasters the meshes drawn into the shadow map, textureMB the GPU texture memory, width and height the size of the picture (design size * window.renderScale). The numbers perf.measure records and perf.check budgets. Throws without graphics. Example: expect(game.renderStats().triangles).toBeLessThan(200000).

members.sig: setAccessibility(settings: { textScale?: number; reduceMotion?: boolean; highContrast?: boolean; screenReader?: boolean }): void
members.doc: Pretends the player's system has these accessibility settings: game.accessibility follows at once. Keys left out are the defaults (textScale 1, the others false); textScale is clamped to 0.5 - 4. An unknown key (with a suggestion), a non-boolean or a textScale that is not a number above 0 throws. Reset to the defaults before every test. Example: game.setAccessibility({ textScale: 1.5, reduceMotion: true }).

Sets the text the next storage load reads, in place of the save file (tests never touch the real storage.json), and drops the data already loaded: storage.get() and storage.corrupt then answer as at a start with that file. Pass a valid JSON object to start from a saved game, or broken text ("{"hi") to test the damaged-save path: storage.corrupt is true and the data is empty. null goes back to an empty storage. Reset before every test file.
The pulses input.vibrate() asked for since the test started, in seconds, oldest first (cleared before each test).
Drives gamepad 0..3 (default 0); a bad index throws. Actions bound to Gamepad* names react like they do to a real pad.
Holds a mouse button (default left) until mouseUp(): input.mouse.down(button) follows. With mouseMove() it tests a drag.
Releases a mouse button held with mouseDown().
Turns the mouse wheel by dy notches for the next frame (input.mouse.wheel); a non-number throws.
True once the game asked to quit during this test (game.quit(), or Back that no input.onBack handler consumed). A test run never stops because of it. Cleared before each test.

Pretends the device has these languages (BCP 47 tags, best first): i18n.systemLanguages answers them so a first-run language choice can be tested. An empty list means no system language. Reset (empty) before each test. Example: game.setSystemLanguages(["es-ES", "en"]).

members.sig: resetState(options?: { storage?: boolean; platform?: boolean; audio?: boolean }): void
members.doc: Resets what the tests of one file share (each file already starts clean): storage clears the save data and any setStorageText text; platform runs platform.reset (nothing bought or unlocked, no scripted answers, no leaderboard scores) and restores the test ad and consent answers; audio stops the music (persist: true included, at once) and every voice, so the next audio.music of the same track starts it again and shows in audioLog(). All default to true; an unknown key throws with a suggestion.

members.sig: checkLayout(options?: { languages?: string[]; textScales?: number[]; uiScales?: number[]; pseudo?: boolean; settleFrames?: number }): { ok: boolean; issueCount: number; issues: { kind: "overflow" | "overlap" | "offscreen" | "tooltip"; scene: string; entity: string; path: string; key: string; text?: string; rect?: number[]; other?: { entity: string; path: string; key: string; text?: string; rect?: number[] }; cases: { language: string; textScale: number; uiScale: number; pseudo: boolean }[] }[]; checked: { scene: string; cases: { language: string; textScale: number; uiScale: number; pseudo: boolean }[] }[] }

It steps a few frames per case (every language x text scale x interface scale) and puts the language, text size and interface scale back. Same options as the command; scenes and steps do not apply. Example: expect(game.checkLayout({ textScales: [1, 2] }).issues).toEqual([]).

members.doc: Presses and releases a mouse button at the position (two steps). Pass a widget id or an Entity instead of a position to use the centre of its laid-out rectangle (safe area included; ui.rectOf): the UI is laid out first, so a panel opened this frame can be clicked at once. Throws, naming the widget, when it is inactive, has no area or is scrolled out of its ScrollList.

members.sig: drag(from: Vec2Like | Entity | string, to: Vec2Like | Entity | string): void
members.doc: Drags with the left mouse button from a position (or the centre of a widget) to another: presses, moves in four steps of one frame each, releases and steps once more (6 steps in all), so a draggable widget's dragStart, dragOver and drop events fire and the click is swallowed. `to` may be any widget (a Panel too) or a position over the world, where the drop reports no target. The path must be longer than the slop of the widget (6 pixels by default), or it is a click.
Loads a scene given as JSON ({ format: "factoria.scene/1", entities: [...] }) instead of a file. `props` is what the scene reads with game.sceneProps(); without it the new scene has {}.

Like a finger on a device it also moves the mouse there and holds the left mouse button (see touchStart). Pass a widget id or an Entity instead of a position to use the centre of its laid-out rectangle (safe area included; ui.rectOf).

members.sig: touchStart(target: Vec2Like | Entity | string, id?: number): void

The first finger also drives the mouse as on a device: the mouse moves to screenPos and the left button goes down (input.mouse.pressed("left") on the first frame), so a script that reads both the mouse and touches sees both. Other fingers do not touch the mouse. Pass a widget id or an Entity instead of a position to use the centre of its laid-out rectangle (safe area included; ui.rectOf).
Moves a finger; the first finger drags the mouse with it.
Lifts a finger; when it is the first finger, the left mouse button is released where it lifted.

members.doc: Saves a PNG of the game (needs graphics). options.scale (0.25 to 4, default 1) renders the same frame at that multiple of the design size, sharp, not upscaled: a 1280x720 game at scale 1.5 gives a 1920x1080 PNG with the same HUD and visible area (store screenshots). options.simulate converts the saved PNG to what a colour-blind viewer sees (greyscale, protanopia, deuteranopia, tritanopia: Machado 2009 matrices, severity 1.0, in linear light on the sRGB pixels) so a test or an AI checks that hazards read without their colour; the player's view (Camera.colorFilter) is not changed.
